contexts.text: The land of Egypt into which he was brought with hooks () = the Scientific through which is falsity.
They sent out hooks to draw them to themselves; like fishermen.
To draw out with hooks of fishing () = by the fallacies of the senses, from which the sensuous man reasons.
All that cast the hook in the stream shall be sad... () = that those who teach will in vain labour by truths to reform the natural man.
I will put a hook in thy jaws () = false-speaking on account of which he is chastised.

I will put my hook in thy nose () = that he will have stupidity and folly; for the nose = perception; and a hook the extraction thereof; properly, immersion into the corporeal Sensuous; which, when separated from the Rational, is stupid.
